JNJ.rationale: JNJ presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. Fundamentally, the company is a high-quality healthcare franchise with strong competitive positioning—AAA credit rating, dual-pillar Innovative Medicine/MedTech model, 75%+ of sales from #1/#2 market positions, and a robust pipeline (10+ assets with $5B+ peak sales potential). TTM revenue of ~$93.7B and net income of ~$26.9B demonstrate scale and profitability. However, trajectory is mixed: Q4 2026 showed only +0.3% QoQ revenue growth and gross profit actually declined -4.4% QoQ, while operating cash flow fell sharply to $2.51B from $9.17B in Q3. The Q1 2025 EPS of $4.54 was inflated by a one-time gain (operating income of $13.63B vs ~$6-7.5B in subsequent quarters), making normalized earnings power lower than the TTM suggests. The Stelara patent cliff is a real headwind, though management raised FY2026 guidance to $100.3-$101.3B revenue and $11.45-$11.65 adjusted EPS, signaling confidence in the new portfolio offsetting losses. On valuation, the stock at $222.51 trades at a P/E of 25.9x—near the top of its 365-day range (16.3-26.8x) and significantly above the ~17-18x level from mid-2025. P/B of 6.7x is also elevated vs the 4.5-7.6x range. This rich valuation relative to its own history caps upside despite solid fundamentals. The recent Q1 earnings beat (sales +9.9% YoY, adjusted EPS $2.70 vs $2.67 est), raised guidance, dividend hike to $1.34/share, and pipeline milestones (IMAAVY FDA Priority Review, Ottava robotic surgery milestone) provide modest near-term catalysts, but the stock has already rallied 47% over 52 weeks, likely pricing in much of this. Talc litigation risk (67,000+ plaintiffs, $6.5B settlement plan) remains an overhang. Net: solid defensive franchise at a premium valuation with modest positive catalysts—mildly attractive.
